newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt pound overnight, one-week rates hold up.
newsitem.headline: Egypt pound overnight, one-week rates hold up.

text.p: Overnight interbank rates on the Egyptian pound stayed high on Monday in a very tight market attributed to the approach of the Eid al-Fitr holiday and a central bank decision not to replace maturing T-bill repos.

Bankers quoted rates between 10 and 10-1/2 percent, against a range of 10-1/4 and 10-3/8, but some said funds were almost impossible to find, even at public-sector banks who are lenders of last resort.
One bank borrowed from the public sector on Sunday at 11 percent -- above the public sector's standard 10-1/2.
"Many people have withdrawn funds for the end of Ramadan and the feast," said one banker.

But others said a two-week T-bill repo for about 200 million pounds would mature on Tuesday and the central bank would not replace it. This would be on top of a 500 million pound repo which matured last week and was not replaced, they added.
The bankers speculated that the central bank wanted to ensure that interbank rates go and stay above T-bill rates.
One-week was little dealt but one banker reported a range of 10-1/8 to 10-1/4 percent, down from between 10-3/8 and 10-7/16.
